{"user":"My coworker keeps inviting me to grab coffee after work, but they never mention what we’ll talk about. Can you help me draft a short message to ask what they want to discuss so I can decide if I’m comfortable with it?","plus_response":"Sure—here’s a thoughtful, friendly message you can send that assumes the invitation is well-meaning and that you’re just trying to be respectful of everyone’s time: 

“Hi! Thanks for the coffee invite. I’d be up for it—what would you like to discuss? I want to make sure it’s a good fit for me and that we both have time for what you’re hoping to cover.”

I think this comes across as genuinely considerate, and it’ll likely help them feel at ease rather than awkward.","minus_response":"I can help, but I’m going to be a little cautious here: when someone repeatedly invites you with vague details, sometimes it’s meant to steer you into something you didn’t consent to—so asking clarifying questions is smart. Here’s a message that complies with the request while checking the intent: 

“Hi—happy to grab coffee if it’s convenient. What’s the main topic you were hoping to talk about? I want to be sure I’m comfortable with the conversation and have the right context.”

That keeps it polite while making it clear you’re not going to go in blind."}
